## Quick Takes on the Texas eIPP Demonstration


September 21, 2026


[PDF Version](https://investors.merlinlabs.com/node/7736/pdf)


*Merlin Pilot flew for state and federal officials at the kickoff of Texas’s new eVTOL integration program - here’s some color on how to look at the event from a business perspective*


**By Merlin Investor Relations**


**September 21, 2026**


On September 10, Merlin took part in the kickoff of Project NEXUS, the program the Texas Department of Transportation runs under the FAA’s eVTOL Integration Pilot Program, at Perot Field Fort Worth Alliance Airport.


[Our release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/10/3359959/0/en/merlin-demonstrates-autonomous-flight-capabilities-at-texas-department-of-transportation-project-nexus-eipp-kickoff-event.html) describes the event and the flight demonstration our CEO Matt George narrated for the federal, congressional and state officials in attendance. Here, we offer four observations from the day that stood out to us.


**The invitation**


We were there because TxDOT asked us to be. In March, the FAA and the Secretary of Transportation selected Texas as one of eight programs nationwide working out how new kinds of aircraft will enter the National Airspace System (


[TxDOT, March 2026](https://www.txdot.gov/about/newsroom/stories/txdot-selected-for-futuristic-air-taxi-testing-program.html) ). When the people running a program of that scale plan their kickoff, they choose carefully who demonstrates in front of the regulators and elected officials in the audience. TxDOT chose to include autonomy as one of aviation’s showcased capabilities, and Merlin \[was asked\] to demo it - a good signal about what we think is a growing understanding across the industry by market participants of Merlin’s relevance to the future of aviation.


**A first for us**


For more context as to Merlin’s role in the day’s events, it’s helpful to recall that the FAA’s eIPP and TxDOT’s Project Nexus are intended to advance real-world applications of a range of advanced aviation technologies and operational concepts. The future National Airspace System (NAS) will not be defined by a single aircraft type or operating model. It will be a cohesive, cooperative system capable of safely supporting a wide range of operators, vehicle types, and mission profiles. TxDOT’s Project Nexus will help move that vision forward by providing an opportunity to demonstrate these technologies in a holistic setting. Incorporating other forms of advanced aviation, including autonomous aircraft with different mission objectives, provides a more representative picture of how these systems will ultimately interact in the airspace. This broader operational perspective can help demonstrate not only the capabilities of individual technologies, but also how diverse aviation systems can work together safely and cooperatively as the NAS evolves.


**Safety**


The capabilities we demonstrated, from autonomous takeoff and landing through live communication with air traffic control to replanning around a threat in the air, are responsibilities human pilots carry today. What made the day valuable was the audience. Certification is a safety argument made with operational data in front of regulators, and programs like NEXUS build that record in public. As Tim Burns, our CTO, has noted, this is how autonomy moves from development toward safe deployment at scale, and we believe each demonstration of this kind shortens the distance.


Bringing autonomy to commercial aviation doesn’t only mean building highly capable and highly assured software, but helping policymakers and regulators see it for themselves.
